outputs.color: brandColor as given: bar and button fill
outputs.onColor: #ffffff or #222222, whichever contrasts more with color

outputs.darkOnFill: #ffffff or #222222, whichever contrasts more with darkFill

narrative.overview:
Every email is a short, friendly note handed across a well-run front desk: whose convention it is, what happened, and the one thing you need, in that order. The system is user-pinned as "simple and modern, lightly distinguishable", in the manner of Airbnb and Booking emails: a white page, one roomy 580px column, the reader's own system font, generous air, and outlined rounded boxes that group the facts. It is light in density and quiet in tone; nothing on the page is decoration.

"Lightly distinguishable" is carried by the tenant's colour and nothing else. It appears in three places: the 48×4 bar under the title, the primary button, and the one figure that matters (an order total, a refund amount, a fallback link). Everything else is neutral ink on white, or white on near-black in dark mode, so any tenant colour, from navy to pale yellow, sits in the same frame without fighting it.

The system replaces a rejected themed "game card" world (a framed card from the convention's deck, dark banner, grey page, Archivo display type). That costume, and the grey-page boxed receipt, are confirmed rejections.
keyCharacteristics: White page, near-black (#161616) in dark mode; one 580px column, no card on a grey page.
System font stack only; bold 32px title over a short brand-colour bar.
16px-radius outlined boxes with a bold box title and hairline rows.
The tenant colour on the bar, the button and one figure; derived for contrast, never assumed.
Tickets as light stubs: who and when, a dashed tear line, the QR on white.
Tables only; degrades to a clean, wide, readable layout where `<style>` is dropped.

rules.name: The Derived Voice Rule
rules.body: The brand colour is input, not output. `brandColors(brand)` returns `color` (bar, button fill), `onColor` (white or on-brand ink, whichever contrasts more), `text` (the colour darkened toward ink in 10% steps until it reaches 4.5:1 on white), `darkText` (lightened toward white until 4.5:1 on the night page), `darkFill` (`color` if it reaches 3:1 on the night page, else `darkText`) and `darkOnFill`. Examples from the build: #1F7A5C keeps itself everywhere with white on fill and lightens to #4c957d as dark text; pale yellow #F5C400 takes ink on fill and darkens to #866e0f as text on white; the ink fallback turns light in dark mode: #e5e5e5 fill with ink text, white figures. Never pick a text or fill colour by eye.

rules.name: The Head-Borne Dark Rule
rules.body: Brand colours are inline styles (Tailwind only knows colours it was compiled with), and an inline style cannot follow the colour scheme. Dark-mode brand values ship once in `<head>` through `brandCss(brand)`: any element carrying the brand colour as text gets the `brand-text` class; any element filled with it (bar, button) gets `brand-fill`.

rules.name: The Three Places Rule
rules.body: The tenant colour appears on the title bar, the primary button and at most one figure or link per email. Neutrals carry everything else.

rules.name: The No Web Font Rule
rules.body: The system stack only. No `@font-face`, no Google Fonts link; a face that only some clients load makes a different email in each.

rules.name: The Size-and-Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is size and bold. No uppercase tracked labels, no italics, no second family.

rules.name: The Tables Only Rule
rules.body: Structure is React Email's `Section`, `Row` and `Column` (tables). No flex, no grid, no absolutely positioned layers.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Grouping is an outline at 1px in the hairline colour, never a shadow, a tinted card or a grey page behind a white card.

rules.name: The Inline Dash Rule
rules.body: Dashed lines are written inline (`border-top: 1px dashed`), never with Tailwind's `border-dashed`: react-email resolves Tailwind's border-style variable once per email, so one `border-dashed` dashes every border in it.

dos: **Do** derive every brand use through `brandColors(brand)` and mark it `brand-text` or `brand-fill` so dark mode follows.
**Do** keep the tenant colour to the bar, the button and one figure or link.
**Do** group facts in one 16px-rounded hairline box with a bold 20px title and hairline rows.
**Do** keep the QR on white with its quiet zone inside the image, in every mode.
**Do** write dashed lines as inline styles.
**Do** check every email at 480px and in dark mode; the wide layout is the no-`<style>` fallback.
donts: **Don't** hard-code a tenant's colour or fall back to Congrem green for a tenant; a tenant without a colour gets neutral ink.
**Don't** load a web font or add a second family.
**Don't** use flex, grid, shadows, or opacity colour modifiers (`bg-white/80` renders as `rgb(… / 80%)`, which older clients drop).
**Don't** return to the themed game card: no framed deck card, dark banner, or grey page behind a white card.
**Don't** add uppercase tracked labels or kickers above the title; the logo and the bar already say whose email it is.
